find: You look closely at a dry bean seed.
replace: You look at and touch a dry bean seed.
why: The keyed answer "It feels hard" is found by touch.

find: To look very closely and notice details.
replace: To use your senses, like looking and touching, to notice details.
why: The journal asks "My seed feels"; observing uses all the senses.

replace: Do not need food or water
why: Matches the living column and stops "a tree does not eat, so it is nonliving".

find: That is why we put two seeds
replace: Then it grows into a plant that makes new seeds, which is how we know it is living. That is why we put two seeds
why: Otherwise the guide's own checklist calls the dry seed nonliving.

replace: zip bags, a permanent marker, scissors for each pair and whiteboards. The sorting cards carry words only, so glue a small picture onto each card
why: The handout says to cut the cards, pairs write names on bags, and the picture cards have no pictures.

find: the sunny window and looks at its two seeds through the bag with a hand lens
replace: the window, out of direct sun, and looks at its two seeds through the bag with a hand lens
why: Lesson 1 put the bags away from direct sun; sealed bags overheat in sun.

find: the sunny window and looks at its two seeds through the bag. The seeds
replace: the window, out of direct sun, and looks at its two seeds through the bag. The seeds
why: The same contradiction in the speaker notes.

find: A labeled picture of an opened lima bean seed: seed coat, baby plant, food (two halves)
replace: Seed coat: the thin skin outside. Food: the two big halves. Baby plant: the tiny plant between them.
why: The slide described a picture that is not there.

find: Yes. It is tiny and pale, about the size of a grain of rice, and it is curved near the small mark on the seed.
replace: Yes. Given water, it grows the root you will see in your bag, then leaves. It is tiny and pale, about the size of a grain of rice. Before you peel the seed, find the small mark: the baby plant lies just under that spot.
why: Gives the evidence that the baby plant is alive; the mark comes off with the seed coat students peel first.

find: A bean seed that looks the same as before has a visible change to record.
replace: If your bean seed looks the same as before, there is nothing to write in your journal.
why: The old statement contradicted itself; the key (false) stays right.

find: Record one change in the sprouting bean in the journal
replace: Record what the sprouting bean looks like today in the journal
why: The lesson accepts "it looks the same", so there may be no change to record. (an objective: course-wide, since objectives are not in a lesson's scope)

find: Have the soaked lima beans, trays, hand lenses and journals ready.
replace: Have ready the soaked lima beans, one dry lima bean, trays, hand lenses, whiteboards, the document camera, and the journals with today's two new pages added.
why: The plan uses all of these.

find: Record one change in our sprouting bean
replace: Record what our sprouting bean looks like today
why: The slide's copy of the objective, changed with it.
